lines.trans: Hello, good day, dear Dmitry Vladimirovich.
Come quickly, our chef is feeling bad here.
It seems he had another stroke.
Vika, wait for me in the car, I will be right back.
A cockroach again, whose dish is it?
It is your dish, respected Chef.
Vitya, they told me that you are feeling bad.
Ah yes, my salary could use a little raise.
From a joke like that there are big problems, is that clear?
I will definitely find out who tricked me like this.
I will punish those guys very strictly.
I give my word, I definitely will not forgive this!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello (on the phone)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ладно, давай быстро иди работать.
examples.trans: Alright, go on and get to work quickly.

examples.text: Давай быстро уезжаем отсюда!
examples.trans: Let us drive away from here quickly!

examples.text: Я в порядке, быстро отпусти меня.
examples.trans: I am fine, let me go quickly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will punish', paired with 'наказывать'.

examples.text: Их накажет история.
examples.trans: History will punish them.

examples.text: Мама его накажет.
examples.trans: Mum will punish him.

examples.text: Наказать слепых?
examples.trans: To punish the blind?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'these', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: И от этого решения зависит всё.
examples.trans: And everything depends on this decision.

examples.text: Вообще-то Кузьма — это наш будущий сын.
examples.trans: Actually, Kuzma is our future son.

examples.text: Настя, потому что это странные имена.
examples.trans: Nastya, because those are strange names.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'guys, lads, kids (plural only)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я очень строго накажу этих ребят.
examples.trans: I will punish those guys very strictly.

examples.text: Ребята, вы где?
examples.trans: Guys, where are you?

examples.text: Ребята с тобой поработают.
examples.trans: The boys will have a word with you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'give', paired with 'дать'.

examples.text: Хорошо, давай, как ты хочешь назвать?
examples.trans: Alright, go ahead, what do you want to name him?

examples.text: А давай сейчас у Макса спросим.
examples.trans: Let us ask Max right now.

examples.text: Поэтому не волнуйся, давай ступай.
examples.trans: So do not worry, go on, step along.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лово'). Common neuter noun meaning 'word' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Иногда нам нужно принимать сложные решения.
examples.trans: Sometimes we need to make difficult decisions.

examples.text: Что же это такое, честное слово!
examples.trans: What on earth is this, honest word!

examples.text: Даю слово, точно не прощу!
examples.trans: I give my word, I definitely will not forgive this!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Да шучу я, это таблетка от желудка, достаточно одной таблетки.
examples.trans: I am joking, this is a pill for the stomach, one pill is enough.

examples.text: Даю слово, точно не прощу!
examples.trans: I give my word, I definitely will not forgive this!

examples.text: Лёля точно придёт!
examples.trans: Lyolya will definitely come!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не понял, а почему именно Кузьма?
examples.trans: I do not understand, why Kuzma specifically?

examples.text: Что, Кузьма тебе тоже не нравится?
examples.trans: What, you do not like Kuzma either?

examples.text: Костя, тебе совсем не угодишь.
examples.trans: Kostya, there is no pleasing you at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.text: Простите, а вы сейчас о чём?
examples.trans: Excuse me, and what are you talking about right now?

examples.text: Дима, пожалуйста, прости меня за всё.
examples.trans: Dima, please forgive me for everything.

examples.text: Простите, вы кто?
examples.trans: Excuse me, who are you?
